LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: RECIPE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do you write clear instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify components of a recipe for information
2. write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss different components of recipes with peers,
2. Team up to play a language game involving role playing various adverbs (of manner) used in recipes with peers,
3. Creativity and Imagination: The learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creative thinking when designing a creative recipe book and organising the various recipes shared in the book.
4. Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner is motivated to learn continuously as they write a recipe on a common cultural food from their community. Values:
5. Unity: This is achieved as the learner cooperates with peers to role play a language game involving adverbs (of manner) used in recipes.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you write clear instructions?
2. what went well and why?
3. what did not go well and why?
4. what can be done differently next time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
